task.name: Nothing verifies that a declared transport can serve the model declared on it, so a wrong choice is accepted, certified, and only visible as failures several layers downstream
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2378
---

**Depends on #2378.** That issue corrects the readiness check so it exercises the capability a model will be asked for rather than a plain completion. This issue extends verification across both transports and has it report that the other transport would have served the model — it builds on that check rather than beside it. Extending a check that still exercises a request shape no phase uses would reproduce the original defect at wider scope: every transport comparison would be drawn from evidence that does not reflect what production sends.

## Why

An operator choosing a transport for a model is making a claim nothing checks: that the transport can
serve that model. The claim is easy to get wrong, expensive when wrong, and invisible either way.

Both transports accept any identifier. A CLI runner passes the model string through to its underlying
tool; an API adapter sends it to the provider. Neither reports that the other would have worked, or
that the chosen one will fail for the capability the model is eligible for. A readiness check exists,
but it probes only API profiles, so declaring a CLI-capable model as API moves it onto the checked
path and away from the working one, and the check then passes it.

The failure that motivated this cost a full day. Two models were declared API on the assumption that
the CLI could not serve them — an assumption formed from the absence of a naming convention, never
tested. The CLI serves them fine; the identifier is passed straight through and needs no suffix. The
API transport rejected every tool-bearing request those models were sent, which broke plan review,
code review and the escalation advisor, and produced a day of investigation into what looked like
model instability.

Nothing in the system could have surfaced this. The configuration was valid, the readiness check
passed, routing selected the models, and the failures appeared several layers downstream as parse
errors. The one fact that would have ended it — that the other transport serves this model — was
never asked for, because no surface asks it.

This is not about one family or one provider. Any model declared on a transport that cannot serve it,
or moved onto a transport that serves it worse, fails the same way and is equally hard to see.

## Example

What an operator gets today when a transport choice is wrong, and what would have ended the
investigation on the first day:

```
today
  check-config       openai/gpt-5.6-sol/api    ✓ ready
  check-providers    openai-gpt-5.6-sol-api    ✓ 4.5s
  run                22 × tool-call 400 → text fallback → parse failure
  diagnosis          one day, by hand-probing the provider

wanted
  openai/gpt-5.6-sol
    declared transport : api
    api      ✗ tools rejected (provider: function tools unsupported with reasoning_effort
                               on /v1/chat/completions)
    cli      ✓ serves this identifier
    → declared transport cannot serve the phases this model is eligible for; cli can
```

## Acceptance criteria

- A declared transport is verified against the model it is declared for, so a combination that cannot
  serve the model's eligible phases is reported rather than accepted.
- Verification covers every transport a model could be served on, not only the one declared, so a
  working alternative is named when the declared one fails.
- The result states which capabilities were exercised on which transport, so a pass distinguishes what
  was demonstrated from what was assumed.
- Where a transport cannot be verified, that is reported as unverified rather than as a pass, and the
  reason it could not be exercised is given.
- The check is available before a run is launched, since its value is preventing a dispatch rather
  than explaining one afterwards.
- A model whose declared transport is verified reads no differently than it does today, so the common
  case gains a guarantee rather than new noise.

## Out of scope

Choosing the transport automatically, or overriding an operator's declaration. An operator may have
reasons to prefer a worse-performing transport; the requirement is that the choice be informed, not
that it be made for them.

handoff.summary: Extended provider readiness from single-transport API probing to grouped declared-plus-alternate transport verification. Each probe now records declared and attempted transport identity, clears transport/model fallbacks before dispatch, classifies unavailable or auth/startup-blocked transports as unverified with reasons, and reports alternate ready transports only when the declared transport is not verified. The check-providers command keeps compact output for verified declared transports and expands only failing/unverified cases with per-transport evidence.

reviews.summary: [openai-gpt-5.5-cli] The cross-transport probe handles API-vs-CLI cases, but it can certify an explicitly declared CLI runner by exercising a different CLI runner. | [anthropic-opus-cli] Transport verification is well-structured and the grouped attempt model satisfies most criteria, but the declared runner is discarded when rebuilding the transport, so a gh-aw profile is probed with the local claude binary and certified as its declared CLI transport.

findings.description: When a profile declares the explicit ghaw CLI runner, check-providers derives the declared CLI attempt from the provider family and runs the claude runner instead, so a ghaw declaration can be reported ready without ghaw being exercised.

A profile declaring the gh-aw CLI transport is probed by rebuilding the transport from the provider family alone, which resolves anthropic plus cli to the local claude binary, so the probe dispatches through claude, records the outcome as the declared-transport attempt, and reports the profile ready even though the gh-aw runner was never exercised.

Every probe now dispatches on both its declared transport and the same-provider alternate unconditionally, so the pre-run check issues roughly twice as many billed agent invocations as before, including real CLI agent runs at each profile's full timeout, with no option to restrict verification to the declared transport.

A failed declared-transport attempt is reclassified from failed to unverified whenever its error text contains any of several short substrings such as 'api key', 'credentials', or '401', so a genuine capability rejection whose message happens to mention a key or carries that number in an identifier is reported as not-exercised rather than as a failure of the declared transport.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 constructs attempts with dataclasses.replace and invokes runners/cli.py::run_agent or runners/api.py::run_api_agent, but both honor fallback configuration. A failed CLI attempt can cross to API through _maybe_run_api_fallback, and both paths can try fallback_models, causing a different transport or model to make the requested attempt appear ready.
  Suggestion: Clear api_fallback and fallback_models on every probe-attempt profile, or reject results whose transport_used/model_used differ from the requested attempt. Add a regression test with configured fallbacks where the requested model or transport fails but the fallback succeeds.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 explicitly maps transport_for ValueError to unverified, but does not enumerate runtime inability cases such as AgentResult.startup_failure for a missing CLI or absent credentials. Classifying those as failed would not satisfy the required distinction between an exercised incompatibility and a transport that could not be exercised.
  Suggestion: Define the runtime conditions that map to unverified, including CLI startup failure and authentication/configuration absence, and test that each retains its reason.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 3 (stale cli/provider mirrors) is retired by Step 2's use of transport_for + mirror_fields_for_transport, but the plan does not say how the existing API-shaped classification rules apply to CLI attempts: _requires_structured_verdict parses result.structured_data/JSON, and the cost-unavailable rule (provider_readiness.py:179) fails a probe when cost_usd is None. A CLI runner that returns text or omits cost would be classified failed/cost-unavailable rather than a genuine transport verdict, which would produce exactly the false alternate-transport signal this story exists to prevent.
  Suggestion: Decide per-transport classification explicitly: keep structured-verdict checking for CLI (it is a real capability signal) but treat missing CLI cost as unverified-with-reason rather than a failure, and add a test for a CLI attempt whose result carries cost_usd=None.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Probe count roughly doubles once alternates are exercised, and CLI attempts spawn real local binaries; providers.py caps concurrency at _MAX_READINESS_WORKERS=4 with no per-attempt timeout, so forge check-providers wall time and spend grow with no stated bound.
  Suggestion: Skip alternate-transport attempts whose executable is absent on PATH (report unverified with that reason) before dispatching, which bounds both cost and runtime without new flags.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 changes ordering/grouping input but the sort key in providers.py:66-80 is built from (role, capability, profile.name, profile.model) and will now collide across the declared/alternate attempts of the same probe.
  Suggestion: Include the attempted transport kind in the order key so grouped attempts render deterministically.

findings.description: Acceptance criteria 3 and 6 conflict. AC3 says the result must state which capabilities were exercised on which transport so a pass distinguishes demonstrated behavior from assumptions, but AC6 says a model whose declared transport is verified should read no differently than it does today. Unless the story defines a separate verbose mode or limits the extra detail to failure cases, both cannot be satisfied at once.

Acceptance criterion 6 appears orphaned. The story's Why/Example sections justify earlier, more accurate verification and reporting of alternative transports, but they do not establish a requirement that the verified common case remain identical to today's output. This introduces an extra UX constraint without corresponding requirement rationale.

finding_registry.description: When a profile declares the explicit ghaw CLI runner, check-providers derives the declared CLI attempt from the provider family and runs the claude runner instead, so a ghaw declaration can be reported ready without ghaw being exercised.

Every probe now dispatches on both its declared transport and the same-provider alternate unconditionally, so the pre-run check issues roughly twice as many billed agent invocations as before, including real CLI agent runs at each profile's full timeout, with no option to restrict verification to the declared transport.

A failed declared-transport attempt is reclassified from failed to unverified whenever its error text contains any of several short substrings such as 'api key', 'credentials', or '401', so a genuine capability rejection whose message happens to mention a key or carries that number in an identifier is reported as not-exercised rather than as a failure of the declared transport.

The declared-only switch is exercised only against a configuration whose profiles are all API-declared, so the case that motivated the flag most directly — a CLI-declared profile whose alternate API probe should be skipped — is asserted nowhere, and a future change that skipped the wrong side of the pair for CLI declarations would still pass the suite.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Extend the existing capability-shaped readiness probe from #2378 so each role/model capability is checked against its declared transport and any same-provider alternate transport. Keep the CLI command output quiet for verified declared transports, and only expand reporting when an attempted or unverified transport changes the operator decision.

steps.description: Model per-transport readiness attempts without changing dispatch policy
steps.details: Add a transport-aware result shape around the existing ReadinessProbe/ReadinessResult flow: include attempted transport kind, declared transport kind, and an unverified status. Stop filtering build_readiness_probes to profile.mode == 'api'; dedupe on role, capability, profile identity, declared transport, model, tools, and phase.

steps.description: Derive and execute declared plus alternate transport probes
steps.details: For each ReadinessProbe, derive same-provider candidate transports using profile.provider_family and transport_for(provider, 'api'|'cli'), preserving the declared transport and recording unavailable transports as unverified with the ValueError reason. Build per-attempt profiles with dataclasses.replace plus mirror_fields_for_transport so provider/cli mirror the TransportSpec, call run_api_agent for api and run_agent for cli, and reuse the existing capability validation, OpenAI tool-shape unsupported classification, throwaway working directory, structured verdict check, and cost-unavailable rule where applicable.

steps.description: Report cross-transport evidence without adding noise to the common case
steps.details: Update cmd_check_providers to consume grouped transport results, keep the existing single-line rendering and pass count when the declared transport is ready, and expand only failures/unverified alternatives to show declared transport, each exercised transport, capability, status, and details. Treat a non-ready declared transport as command failure; name any ready alternate transport in the expanded detail. Update parser/help text and --profile not-found wording from API-only to provider capability checks.

steps.description: Cover readiness behavior and CLI output contract with deterministic tests
steps.details: Update existing API-only tests for the new probe/result shape; add tests for CLI-declared profiles being exercised, API-declared failure naming a ready CLI alternate, alternate transport unavailable being reported unverified with a reason, exercised capability/transport appearing in expanded output, and verified declared transports retaining the old compact output. Patch provider_readiness.run_agent in conftest like run_api_agent so default tests never invoke real provider CLIs.

criteria_mapping.criterion: A declared transport is verified against the model it is declared for, so a combination that cannot serve the model's eligible phases is reported rather than accepted.
Verification covers every transport a model could be served on, not only the one declared, so a working alternative is named when the declared one fails.
The result states which capabilities were exercised on which transport, so a pass distinguishes what was demonstrated from what was assumed.
Where a transport cannot be verified, that is reported as unverified rather than as a pass, and the reason it could not be exercised is given.
The check is available before a run is launched, since its value is preventing a dispatch rather than explaining one afterwards.
A model whose declared transport is verified reads no differently than it does today, so the common case gains a guarantee rather than new noise.

risks.description: This issue depends on #2378; if the branch does not already contain the corrected capability-shaped probe, extending readiness would still compare the wrong request shape.
risks.mitigation: Rebase after #2378 lands and reuse the existing capability prompt/request path rather than adding a parallel readiness request.

risks.description: CLI readiness probes can accidentally invoke real CLIs in tests or contributor gates.
risks.mitigation: Keep tests patched at provider_readiness.run_agent/run_api_agent and add the conftest guard before adding CLI execution paths.

risks.description: Transport mutation can leave stale cli/provider mirrors if only transport is replaced.
risks.mitigation: Use transport_for plus mirror_fields_for_transport when constructing alternate profiles, matching existing ModelProfile transport conventions.
